correctness.rationale: The edge Fourier decomposition yields uniformly finite positive radii for p<2. At each facet normal the transverse-edge terms vary O(theta); parallel distinct-edge cross terms are o(|theta|^(2-p)) by Riemann–Lebesgue, while self terms give the exact positive length^(4-p) coefficient using an explicitly evaluated sinc Mellin integral. Non-Lipschitz reciprocal radius contradicts the support-function identity for a hypothetical convex star. For p>=2 positive self terms force divergence at each facet normal. The independent triangle divided-difference Fourier calculation, the published square coefficient, an exact projected-vertex trapezoid calculation with unequal parallel edges, and a numerical Mellin identity all agree. Limits to all polygons rest on analytic proof, not finite sampling.
